up.note: Fact 2. If $p/q = f$ on the domain then $(q-2p)q$ is a sign representation: it equals $-q^2 < 0$ where $f = 1$ and $q^2 > 0$ where $f = 0$. The factor $2$ is not removable -- $\deg_{\pm}(\oplus_n) = n$ while $\mathrm{rdeg}(\oplus_n) = n/2$. Only the identity $p/q = f$ on the domain is used, so the bound holds on promises as well, and is recorded here for the partial setting so that the total one inherits it.

  • \(\deg_{\pm}(\oplus_n) = n = 2\,\mathrm{rdeg}(\oplus_n)\)
    witness: \(\oplus_n\) KKWY26
    The factor of $2$ in the upper bound is attained, so the cell is settled at exponent $1$ and the constant is settled too.

Nothing travels the other way: majority has a degree-$1$ sign representation, while $\mathrm{D} = n$ together with $\mathrm{D} = O(\mathrm{rdeg}\deg_{\pm}^2\log n)$ forces $\mathrm{rdeg}(\mathrm{MAJ}_n) = \Omega(n/\log n)$ -- Remark 2 of [KKWY26], where majority is what shows Theorem 8 tight up to the log.

Sign degree is the one measure the new bound treats as a second parameter rather than a corollary: $\mathrm{D} \le 4\deg_{\pm}^2\mathrm{rdeg}^2$ and $\deg = \widetilde O(\deg_{\pm}^2\mathrm{rdeg})$ are both stronger than their pure-$\mathrm{rdeg}$ consequences, and $\deg_{\pm}$ is not polynomially related to $\deg$ at all (majority again). See also Corollary 5 of [KKWY26], which replaces $\mathrm{rdeg}$ by $\mathbb{F}_2$-degree in the same slot: two measures that are each incomparable to $\deg$ multiply to bound it, the way $\deg \le \mathrm{C}^0\mathrm{C}^1$ does.

see also: \(\mathrm{sdeg}(f)\), \(\mathrm{rdeg}(f)\), \(\oplus_n\), \(\mathrm{MAJ}_n\), \(\deg(f)\) data/relations/02-degree.yaml
